label: caiso 69 sp15split dragoff
definition: (PROBE — pre-registered A/B, negative result) SP15-split main -- caiso-68 recipe (caiso65 keeper config + temp_dependent_derate) on the LA_BASIN/SDGE/SP15_rest split topology, ct_netload_drag=False per-run override, 2023-2025 RESULT: pocket links bind (SDGE ~1,000-1,240 h/yr at its 1,436 MW cap, LA 0-256 h) but form only ~$1-4 mean premium; CT_PEAKER collapses to 0.79-0.94 TWh without the drag (vs 1.56-2.10 with it; actual 3.09-5.24): the split alone cannot carry CT dispatch. 2023 hrs>$200 530 vs actual 21 (unchanged — stack-top gas, not copperplate). C8 forced-share FAIL->PASS (D-2 CT drag share 56/53/55% -> 0.8/1.4/0.0%, RA-bridge remnant only), C5a FAIL->CAVEAT, C7 PASS->FAIL (merit CT profile_r 0.76/0.76/0.68 vs 0.8 gate — the drag was carrying CT's diurnal shape). SCORING CORRECTION (2026-07-09, supersedes this sidecar's original text and the A/B LMP targets in both SP15-split handoff docs): the 'actual SP15 $118-127' those targets quoted was a misread of the run payload's lmp[zone].d field, which is the dashboard demand WEIGHT (sum of monthly mean zonal load in GW — backcast-runs.html ~line 331 uses it as the LMP weighting), not a price; the same misread would make ZP26's 'actual' $14. Measured DA hub actuals (data/raw/lmp-data/CAISO, groupby node mean) are SP15 $49.39/$32.68/$32.22 and NP15 $51.26/$40.67/$38.23 (2023/24/25) — so the model OVER-prices the SoCal pockets by ~$15-21 (model $47-71) and actual SP15 clears BELOW NP15 (+$1.9/+$8.0/+$6.0 NP15-SP15); there is no missing $48-78 premium to close. The earlier redirect ('offer level above SRMC + tighter-than-LCT local limits') is therefore wrong-directional — raising SoCal offers or tightening pocket limits would worsen an existing overshoot. Corrected redirect: the CT gap is a commitment/AS-dispatch question, not a price-level one — note the zero-forcing ablation clears MORE CT than this run (2.02/1.41/0.98 vs 0.90/0.91/0.79 TWh), i.e. the RA bridge's forced CC min-gen crowds peakers out of the very pockets that should call them; reserve/AS co-optimization dispatching CTs (RTPD/RUC-like) is the missing forward-real driver. Not promotable (7 fails incl. C7); the split topology itself is structurally sound (links bind with measured LCT caps, zero fitted parameters) and worth keeping under a future commitment-side fix.
